rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes annealing to enhance oxide formation, while the target uses nanoindentation/friction simulation at different temperatures without any annealing step. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature wear testing at 200-600°C with a load of 10 N and sliding speed of 0.1 m/s, whereas the target uses nanoindentation/friction simulation at 300-1200 K with a virtual indenter at 10 m/s. The temperature ranges overlap only partially, and the testing methods and loading conditions are completely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a stable oxide-based tribofilm reducing metal-to-metal contact, while the target's mechanism involves lattice disorder, dislocation density evolution, and stacking fault to disorder transition. These are entirely different classes of mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved wear resistance and reduced friction at high temperatures, whereas the target predicts stable wear resistance up to 600 K then a sharp decrease above 900 K with increased friction. The predicted directions are opposite.
